title: Tag lexicon
description: Tag master data: one entity per tag, where the key is an internal stable identifier kept separate from display names. The database stores keys and the UI resolves them against the current language, so switching languages never affects filtering. You can edit the lexicon file directly and press "Reload" to apply it; names you have not customized come from the built-in table. The list is filtered by the selected editing language: by default only entities that already have a name in that language are shown; switch the scope to "Missing … name" to fill in translations.

merge.title: Merge "{{name}}" into another entry
merge.description:
Every name and source clue of this entry moves into the target, and its own key becomes a redirect (existing game data keeps resolving). Use it when this entry should not exist on its own; if only a source points at the wrong place, use "Fix index".
Note: a language can only have one display name. When both sides have one, pick a target and then choose "Keep" or "Overwrite" per language in the "Name preview" ("Keep" by default).
merge.targetPlaceholder: Pick the entry to merge into

preview.title: Name preview (after merging)
preview.customPlaceholder: Type the name to use for this language
preview.supersededWarn: {{count}} language(s) have more than one spelling: "Keep" uses the current one, "Overwrite" switches to another entry's spelling; a struck-out one is dropped. Change any of them above.

merge.titleMulti: Merge the {{count}} selected entries into one
merge.descriptionMulti:
The names and source indexes of the selected entries move into the target, and each of the others gets its own redirect (existing game data keeps resolving).
Pick which one is the target above (the last one you clicked by default). A language can only have one display name, so when a language has more than one spelling, choose "Keep" or "Overwrite" per language in the "Name preview" ("Keep" by default).

move.title: Fix source index
move.description: Repoints the selected source index of "{{name}}" at the correct entry. Both entries stay; scanning that source resolves to the target from now on.
move.sources: Source index to fix (per source, as a block)
move.noSources: This entry has no source index left to fix: it may already have been fixed or detached, or it all comes from the built-in table.
move.namesStayHint: Fixing the index only moves source entries — translations stay on this entry. If the target is missing a language, add it by hand on the lexicon page.
move.targetPlaceholder: Pick the entry the index should point to

notification.builtinOnly: These sources come from the built-in lexicon and cannot be changed: it is authoritative code data and would be restored on the next refresh.
notification.partiallyBlocked: {{count}} of them come from the built-in lexicon; only the part in your own lexicon was moved.
notification.shellHint: "{{name}}" no longer has any source clue — you can delete it or merge it elsewhere.

migrate.title: Convert stored tags into keys
migrate.description: Old tags in the library still hold the raw text from the scrape, while filtering matches the stored value exactly — so "new data holding a key" and "old data holding text" are two different values to a filter. This rewrites the raw text into tag keys: what the lexicon recognises is merged into the existing tag, the rest can be added as new tags.
migrate.mintUnknown: Add the unrecognised ones as new tags
migrate.mintUnknownHint: Checked, they become {{count}} user tags named after the raw text; a later scan of a similar tag lands in the conflict centre for you to merge. Unchecked, they stay exactly as they are.
migrate.willChange: {{count}} tag values will be rewritten. This writes straight into the game documents — back up the database first.
